questions.prompt: Python is called an interpreted language. What does that mean in practice?
choices: You must compile it to a .exe before running it
It reads and runs your code line by line, with no separate compile step
It only runs inside a web browser
It converts your code to English first
questions.explain: An interpreter executes each instruction as it reaches it, so you can run a file the moment you have saved it.

questions.prompt: Why is Python often recommended as a first language?
choices: It is the fastest language available
Its syntax reads close to plain English, so you spend more time on ideas than punctuation
It is the only language that can do maths
It hides your mistakes from you
questions.explain: Readable syntax means less of your attention goes on the language itself and more on the problem.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT something Python is commonly used for?
choices: Rendering the pixels in a graphics card driver
questions.explain: Low-level driver code is written in languages closer to the hardware. Everything else on this list is everyday Python.

reflection1.hint: Name the thing you want to be able to do, not just the word Python. "Build" or "automate" plus what you would build or automate is enough.

reflection2.hint: Say what about the language itself makes it easier to start with. The syntax, or what is available once you know it.
